name: Example: Completing the Mean Value Theorem Statement From the Graph of a Function
problem:
The function $y=f(x)$ below is continuous on $[-1,4]$ and differentiable on $(-1,4).$  Complete the sentence below.

*The mean value theorem states that there exists a point $c \in (-1,4)$ such that $\_\_\_\_\_\_ \, .$ *

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14074895/assets/5672cc68e55078623f34f01650d3e82bd3cee62e6ca97fabcd2287f2a865501a.png)
worked_solution:
Given that $f(x)$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b),$ the mean value theorem states the following:

*There exists a point $c \in (a,b)$ such that
$f'(c) = \dfrac {f(b) - f(a)} {b-a}.$*

In our case, we have $a = -1$ and $b=4,$ so the above statement becomes 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(4)-f(-1)}{4-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{6-2}{4+1} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the complete sentence is as follows:

*The mean value theorem states that there exists a point $c \in (-1,4)$ such that* $f'(c) =\dfrac {4}{5}.$
